title: Major Works of Hispanic Literature in Translation
description: A study of major works selected from the best of Spanish and Spanish-American literature. A knowledge of Spanish is not required. CA 1. CA 4-INT.

title: Christians, Muslims and Jews in Medieval Spain
description: Contacts, conflicts and coexistence among the diverse cultures and traditions of medieval Spain: Christian Hispania, Muslim al-Andalus, and Jewish Sefarad. Taught in English. CA 1. CA 4-INT.

title: Latino Literature, Culture, and Society
description: Critical approaches to Latinos/as and cultural representation, production, and agency, as impacted by globalization and local dynamics. Will engage the value and function of  race, gender and sexuality in popular culture, literature, film, music, digital culture, visual arts, and urban culture.  Taught in English. Knowledge of Spanish is not required. CA 1. CA 4.

title: Contemporary Spanish Culture and Society through Film
description: Critical approaches to Spanish culture and society from the early 20th century to the present as portrayed in Spanish film. Introduction to filmic textual analysis and film history. Discussion of topics such as the avant-garde, social art, revolutionary movements, civil war, exile, Francoism, democratic transition, peripheral nationalisms, immigration, cultural diversity, postmodernity, globalization. Taught in English; Spanish not required; does not fulfill foreign language requirement. CA 1. CA 4-INT.

title: Contemporary Spanish Culture and Society through Film
description: Critical approaches to Spanish culture and society from the early 20th century to the present as portrayed in Spanish film. Introduction to filmic textual analysis and film history. Discussion of topics such as the avant-garde, social art, revolutionary movements, civil war, exile, Francoism, democratic transition, peripheral nationalisms, immigration, cultural diversity, postmodernity, globalization. Taught in English; Spanish not required; does not fulfill foreign language requirement. CA 1. CA 4-INT.

title: Spanish for Engineering II
requirements: SPAN 3101 or instructor consent; open to sophomore or higher dual-degree Spanish and Engineering students. Not open for credit to students who have passed SPAN 3171. Recommended preparation: SPAN 1003 or equivalent.
description: This course provides dual-degree Engineering and Spanish students more advanced vocabulary, methods, and field-specific knowledge. Students will learn to describe scientific processes, to follow scientific presentations in Spanish, and to create preparation and evaluation materials for these presentations.

title: Spanish for the Health Professions
requirements: SPAN 1004 or three or more years of Spanish in high school.
description: Introduction to medical terminology and language uses in Spanish for students desiring to use Spanish in the health professions. Intercultural preparation to work with patients of Latino and Hispanic origin.

title: Intermediate Spanish Composition
requirements: SPAN 1004 or three or more years of Spanish in high school.
description: Provides a thorough review of grammar and methodical practice in composition leading to command of practical idioms and vocabulary.

title: Intermediate Spanish Composition
requirements: SPAN 1004 or three or more years of Spanish in high school.
description: Provides a thorough review of grammar and methodical practice in composition leading to command of practical idioms and vocabulary.

title: Spanish Conversation: Cultural Topics
requirements: Recommended preparation: SPAN 3178 or instructor consent.
description: In-depth development of speaking skills through cultural readings, group discussions and oral presentations on selected topics concerning the Spanish-speaking world.

title: Spanish Civilization to the Modern Period
requirements: Recommended preparation: SPAN 3178 or instructor consent.
description: An interdisciplinary course analyzing the politics, social structures, and cultural life of Spain from its beginnings to the start of the nineteenth century.

title: Contemporary Spain
requirements: Recommended preparation: SPAN 3178 or instructor consent.
description: An interdisciplinary course analyzing the politics, social structures and cultural life in Spain today. Spain in relation to Western Europe and the community of nations.

title: Women's Studies in Spanish
requirements: Recommended preparation: SPAN 3178 or instructor consent.
description: Women in Spanish and Ibero-American literature. Women's writings. The development of Spanish and Ibero-American feminism. Contemporary issues concerning women in the Spanish-speaking world.

title: Issues in Hispanic Thought: Decolonial Theory and Creative Practice
requirements: Recommended preparation: SPAN 3178 or instructor consent.
description: Selection for study of a major world issue debated in the Iberian Peninsula or in Ibero-America by great thinkers. A history of the issue, taking into account international cultural contexts.

title: Topics in Hispanic Cultures
requirements: Recommended Preparation: five semesters of college Spanish.
description: Selected topics. Cross-disciplinary approach to the study of Peninsular and Hispanic American cultures: the colonial heritage in Latin America; intellectual traditions and national identities; cultural production under military regimes; and experience of exiles; among possible topics.

title: Introduction to Literary Study
requirements: Recommended preparation: SPAN 3178 or instructor consent.
description: Introduction to literary analysis through a variety of critical approaches: readings in poetry, drama, and prose fiction with explanation of terms useful to the study of literature.

title: Great Works of Spanish Literature from its Origins to the Golden Age
requirements: Recommended preparation: SPAN 3178 or instructor consent.
description: The study of selected poems, plays, fables and novels reflecting the development of Spanish society from feudalism to world empire.

title: Literature of Crisis in Modern Spain
requirements: Recommended preparation: SPAN 3178 or instructor consent.
description: The study of selected poems, plays, short fiction, and novels reflecting the clash between tradition and progress in nineteenth- and twentieth-century Spain. CA 1.

title: Advanced Spanish Composition
requirements: ENGL 1007 or 1010 or 1011. Recommended preparation: SPAN 3178.
description: Treatment of the finer points of Spanish grammar. Exercises in translation and free composition. Stylistic analysis of texts chosen from Spanish or Latin American authors, newspapers, and magazines.

title: Film in Spain and Latin America
description: Film language and genre in Spanish and Latin American cinema. Taught in English. CA 1. CA 4-INT.

title: Studies in Spanish-American Literature
requirements: Recommended Preparation:  SPAN 3201
description: Readings and discussions of specific aspects of Spanish-American literature. Consult department for particulars each year.

title: Literature of Puerto Rico and the Spanish Caribbean
requirements: Recommended preparation: SPAN 3178 or instructor consent.
description: Readings and discussions of major authors and works of the Spanish Caribbean with special emphasis on Puerto Rico.

title: The Spanish-American Short Story
requirements: ENGL 1007 or 1010 or 1011. Recommended preparation: SPAN 3178.
description: Readings of major authors and works with special emphasis on the development of the short story since the nineteenth century and on its relations to other short narrative forms (such as the fable, the cuadro de costumbres, or the tradición) as well as to significant moments of Spanish-American social history. CA 1.

title: Studies in Spanish Literature
description: May be repeated for up to nine credits with a change of topic.

title: Special Topics
requirements: Open to students in the MSW program.
description: Introduces new and innovative material into the curriculum on an experimental basis. Any special topics course may be offered only twice and may not duplicate content already available in the regular curriculum. Any instructor offering a special topics course must submit the title and a brief statement of focus of the course to the Registrar for inclusion in the course registration schedule. A student may apply up to eight credits of Independent Study and Special Topics in Social Work (combined) toward the M.S.W. degree.

title: Research IV: Multivariate Statistics II
requirements: SSW 6412; open to doctoral students in Social Work, others with consent.
description: Building upon SSW 6412, focuses on the selection and application of appropriate statistical procedures to answer research questions or test hypotheses in social work research. Data reduction methods and analyses of discrete or categorical data and involves the extensive use of available statistical packages. While the course emphasizes the understanding of statistical testing, interpretation and written presentation of statistical results, knowledge of the mathematical formulae and assumptions underlying each statistical procedure may be required, and these are discussed in class.

title: Research V: Qualitative Research Methods
requirements: SSW 6410; SSW 6411, which may be taken concurrently; open to doctoral students in Social Work, others with consent.
description: Philosophical underpinnings, history, techniques and relevance to social work research of qualitative inquiry traditions such as biography, phenomenology, grounded theory, ethnography and case study methods. Although many of these techniques are also useful in social work practice, this course will focus on the use of qualitative methods for the purpose of expansion of the knowledge base of the profession. As such the course will emphasize techniques, standards of quality, verification, and other indicators of rigor as well as value an ethical issues. After completing this course students will be able to describe various approaches, set up research protocols, utilize qualitative data analysis software (e.g. NVivo), describe quality control techniques and specify standards for report writing.

title: Topics in Advanced Social Work Research
requirements: SSW 6410; open only to doctoral students in Social Work, others with permission.
description: Advanced content on variable topics in social work research. Offers advanced conceptual understanding of skills used in complex research design, measurement, and or/analysis. Topics may include mixed methods research, advanced translational research, advanced quantitative analysis, advanced qualitative analysis, or other specialized research methods critical to the field of social work.

title: Social Welfare Policy Seminar
requirements: Open to doctoral students in Social Work, others with permission.
description: Focuses on the concepts, methods, and practices of analysis of social welfare policies designed to address social problems in the United States. Students are expected to apply social science research training and critical thinking skills to study the ideological and socioeconomic contextual backgrounds of social problems, social policies, and policy analyses and evaluate various alternatives to problem definitions, policy strategies, and types of policy analysis. Helps students develop advanced skills in analyzing and critiquing social welfare policies and programs, making recommendations for change, and effectively communicating the results of their work.

title: Introduction to Statistics I
requirements: Students can receive no more than four credits from STAT 1000Q and 1100Q. Students who have passed a 2000-level or above STAT course or who are taking such a course concurrently cannot take 1000-level STAT courses.
description: A standard approach to statistical analysis primarily for students of business and economics; elementary probability, sampling distributions, normal theory estimation and hypothesis testing, regression and correlation, exploratory data analysis. Learning to do statistical analysis on a personal computer is an integral part of the course.

description: Statistics essential for data science incorporating descriptive statistics; integrative numerical description and visualization of data; graphical methods for determining and comparing distributions of data; data-driven statistical inference of one-sample, two-sample, and k-sample problems; linear regression;  non-linear regression; and dependent data models.

requirements: Open to graduate students in the MS in Data Science program, others with permission. Introductory course in mathematical and applied statistics; introductory course in programming.

title: Applied Statistics II
requirements: BIST/STAT 5505.
description: Analysis of variance, regression and correlation, analysis of covariance, general liner models, robust regression procedures, and regression diagnostics.

title: Bayesian Data Analysis
requirements: STAT 5585 and 5685; or instructor consent.
description: Theory of statistical inference based on Bayes' Theorem: basic probability theory, linear/nonlinear, graphical, and hierarchical models, decision theory, Bayes estimation and hypothesis testing, prior elicitation, Gibbs sampling, the Metropolis-Hastings algorithm, Monte Carlo integration.

Health Systems Science (HSS) 1.1 Teaching Longitudinal
description:
The health systems science program is a suite of courses that complement the study of the basic and clinical sciences and represent the third critical domain to prepare clinicians for practice in the twenty-first century.  Health systems science introduces students to the analytical tools and skills they need to understand health policy and the health care system, apply a systems-based approach to dilemmas within the health care system, assess the scientific literature, measure population health, and advocate for greater health equity for all their patients. In addition to building a set of skills, students will apply them to important issues, including patient safety and quality improvement, use of population health data sources, and high value care. The courses also give students direct experiences meeting and working with patients living with challenging and/or chronic illnesses, exploring local communities and work environments that shape the social determinants of health, identifying community resources and organizations, and learning from a wide variety of other health professionals in their practice settings. 
Health systems science utilizes a variety of pedagogies, including team-based learning (TBL), problem-based learning (PBL), interprofessional education, applied projects, patient-experience panels, and experiences in the community and at our affiliate institutions to fully equip our students as life-long learners and teachers.

Focus on plays and performances, primarily from the 20th- and 21st-century United States, analyzing how evolving feminist concerns are reflected in women's theatrical work and how changing concepts of gender and other intersectional identities are embodied on the stage. CA 4.

title: Genders and Sexualities
description: Intersectional examination of diverse constructions of gender and sexuality. Focused exploration of selected topics.

title: Gender Representations in U.S. Popular Culture
description: Forces in the U.S. that shape and reshape gender in popular culture. CA 2.

title: Women and Gender in the Deaf World
requirements: Recommended preparation: Any 1000 or 2000-level WGSS course.
description: The roles of women inside and outside the Deaf world. How language and cultural barriers perpetuate the roles defined for and by d/Deaf women within Deaf and hearing societies.

title: Feminist, Queer, and Trans Theories
requirements: Recommended preparation: WGSS 2250.
description: Exploration of foundational and current critical theory in feminist, queer, and trans studies. May offer an intermediate-level survey of theoretical perspectives or be structured around a theme.

title: Feminist Disability Studies
requirements: ENGL 1007 or 1010 or 1011; open to juniors or higher; sophomores by consent of instructor. Recommended preparation: any 1000 or 2000-level WGSS course.
description: Social, historical, cultural, and political constructions of the intersecting categories of gender and disability. Through a wide variety of texts and cultural examples, exploration of how disability is gendered, gender is disabled, and both are interwoven by race, ethnicity, class, nationality, sexuality, and subcultures.

title: Latina Narrative
description: Feminist topics in contemporary Latina literature and cultural studies.

title: Gender, Sexuality, and Social Movements
requirements: Recommended preparation: Any 1000 or 2000 level WGSS course.
description: Examination of social movements as related to intersections of gender, race, sexuality, disability, class, nationality, ethnicity. May include related topics such as capitalism, democracy, globalization, economic justice, the environment, health, sexual freedom.

title: Seminar on Rape Education and Awareness I
description: Explores issues of sexual violence and trains those enrolled to facilitate rape awareness workshops for the campus community. Students are required to attend an intensive two-day training program and participate in weekly seminars.

title: Anthropological Perspectives on Women
description: Major conceptual and historical problems in the study of gender in anthropology. Women's roles in different historical and contemporary settings, and new understandings of family, kinship, power, and cultural ideologies.

title: Women's Literature 1900 to the Present
description: Modern and contemporary works written by women from different countries. CA 4.

title: Feminism and Science Fiction
description: Feminist approaches to science fiction. Human and non-human embodiments - humans, aliens, and cyborgs - and the social issues their interactions raise: reproduction and colonization; racial, sexual, and gender apartheid; "human" rights and the rule of law. CA 4.

title: Internship Program
requirements: One WGSS course.
description: A field placement in an organization related to the student's major field of study. Work is overseen by the field work supervisor and the Women's, Gender, and Sexuality Studies Internship Coordinator.

title: Variable Topics: Embodying Feminisms
requirements: Prerequisites and recommended preparation vary.

title: Variable Topics: Intro. Native Amer. & Indigen
requirements: Prerequisites and recommended preparation vary.

title: Capstone Seminar
requirements: ENGL 1007 or 1010 or 1011; WGSS 2250; Open to Women's, Gender, and Sexuality Studies majors only. Open to seniors; juniors by consent of instructor. Recommended preparation: WGSS 3265W.
description: Synthesis of studies in the discipline, including discussion of major concerns and topics in WGSS research and praxis. Exploration of post-graduate pathways intersecting with students’ interests and goals and application of feminist research methods and theories to a research project.

title: Critical Epistemologies and Methodologies
description: Theoretical underpinnings of critical methodologies and interdisciplinary research including feminist, queer, trans, critical race, post-colonial, indigenous and disability studies. Contemporary debates and ethical dilemmas faced by researchers using critical feminist, interdisciplinary and intersectional epistemologies. Guided experience in designing and producing critical course outlines and course assignments.

title: Variable Topics in Women's, Gender, and Sexuality Studies: Historical Women Political Thinkers
description: With a change in topics, may be repeated for credit.
